A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same universal-approximation framework and contain readable theorem statements, equations, and Appendices A–C. The title revision and added checklist in v2 do not limit comparison.

before.justification: v1 presents theoretical results and proofs, including architecture-specific applications, but no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical throughout the main text and appendices. Its added checklist explicitly states that the paper includes no experiments.

M1.justification: The transformer formulation, attention mechanisms, and proposed biased and symmetry-preserving architectures remain unchanged. The additional literature discussion introduces no method component.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or tasks for empirical training or evaluation. Newly mentioned application domains and variable-length formulations are contextual discussion, not evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates empirical baselines. Additional cited architectures and theoretical comparisons in v2 belong to related work.

E3.justification: Neither version reports an experimental protocol, evaluation metrics, data splits, or training budgets. The added checklist supplies no such settings.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies, or empirical case studies are added or removed. The architecture examples and their theoretical analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experiments, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Gaussian-weight assumptions in the retained proofs are not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Neither version reports empirical measurements or qualitative experimental findings. The stated UAP conclusions for the architecture examples also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The theorem statements, assumptions, and equations are retained, but Appendix B.1, Step 2 changes its invoked result from Proposition 1 to Proposition 3. This introduces a localized proof-dependency inconsistency: Proposition 1 supplies the stated sequence-level interpolation and bound, whereas Proposition 3 concerns interpolation in R^d.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the same unified sufficient condition, analytic two-sample verification, attention-layer guarantees, and applications to existing and proposed architectures. Abstract and conclusion edits do not materially change these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 2.2 newly clarifies the fixed-length, compact-domain scope and its relationship to variable-length measure-theoretic formulations. Section 5 adds that the non-constructive framework does not quantify individual components' contributions to approximation efficiency; the normalization and analyticity limitations are retained.

D1.justification: No implementation instructions, hyperparameters, computing resources, or code/data access information are added. The checklist marks experimental reproducibility and resource questions inapplicable.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 and Appendix A substantially broaden positioning through comparisons with generic equivariant controllability, measure-theoretic transformer results, and attention-only UAP. A new paragraph covers transformer variants and parameter-efficient fine-tuning. All earlier references are retained, with 19 works added.

P1.justification: v2 revises the title and author order, makes localized wording corrections, expands explanatory paragraphs, renames Summary to Conclusion, and appends a NeurIPS checklist. The existing scientific narrative and section organization largely remain intact.

P2.justification: The single-column format is retained, with no figures or tables in either version. v2 changes the title-page author arrangement and conference footer, reflows text and equations, and adds the formatted checklist.

improvement.justification: The expanded comparisons and explicit scope and quantitative limitations in Section 2.2, Section 5, and Appendix A improve readers' understanding of what the unchanged results establish. Appendix B.1 introduces an incorrect proposition reference, reducing proof traceability, but the required Proposition 1 remains present. The clarification benefits outweigh this localized defect without constituting a substantial scientific improvement.
